definition.limitation: Energy ratio from 200-500 Hz. This is a descriptive band measure, not proof that the sound is boxy.
Counts samples at or beyond full scale; cannot identify upstream clipping below full scale.
Whole-interval sample-peak to RMS ratio.
Mean sample value across all channels.
Energy ratio from 2-5 kHz. Perceived harshness depends on source, level, masking, and time structure.
Energy above 4 kHz in the time-averaged mono spectrum.
ITU-R BS.1770-5 gated K-weighted programme loudness. Short isolated tracks can be perceptually atypical programme material.
Energy below 250 Hz in the time-averaged mono spectrum.
Maximum of 400 ms K-weighted blocks; it is not a phrase-level or short-term 3 s measure.
Energy from 250 Hz to 4 kHz in the time-averaged mono spectrum.
Sample peak, not oversampled true peak.
Mean normalized positive magnitude change between adjacent analyzed frames.
Ungated whole-interval RMS; not integrated loudness.
Energy ratio from 5-10 kHz. A vocal detector is required before interpreting it as sibilance.
Whole-interval RMS of the same linked complementary 6.5 kHz upper split used by the deterministic de-esser. It calibrates detector level but does not identify phonemes or prove sibilance.
Mean power spectrum over Hann-windowed mono fold-down frames; source separation and masking are not represented.
Geometric-to-arithmetic mean of the averaged power spectrum; not a direct noise or quality score.
Frequency below which 85% of averaged spectral energy lies.
Unweighted linear fit to log-frequency power; do not treat a particular slope as universally correct.
Zero-lag whole-interval Pearson correlation; frequency-dependent phase is not represented.
Flux outlier count per second; tempo and event type are not inferred.

ITU-R BS.1770-5 Annex 2 FIR at 48 kHz; other rates use a bounded windowed-sinc estimate at >=192 kHz and >=2x. The meter is not formally conformance-tested and can under-read between evaluated phases.

crest_factor_timeline.limitation: Windowed sample-peak/RMS ratio; it does not by itself prove punch, over-compression, or quality.

positive_spectral_flux_timeline.limitation: Normalized positive magnitude flux on selected Hann-windowed mono fold-down frames. Long captures use a larger effective hop, and anti-phase stereo can cancel; it indicates change, not event identity or quality.

rms_dbfs_timeline.limitation: 200 ms windowed RMS with 50% nominal overlap; phrase and source interpretation require musical context.

definition.limitation: Energy ratio from 200-500 Hz. This is a descriptive band measure, not proof that the sound is boxy.
Counts samples at or beyond full scale; cannot identify upstream clipping below full scale.
Whole-interval sample-peak to RMS ratio.
Mean sample value across all channels.
Energy ratio from 2-5 kHz. Perceived harshness depends on source, level, masking, and time structure.
Energy above 4 kHz in the time-averaged mono spectrum.
ITU-R BS.1770-5 gated K-weighted programme loudness. Short isolated tracks can be perceptually atypical programme material.
Energy below 250 Hz in the time-averaged mono spectrum.
Maximum of 400 ms K-weighted blocks; it is not a phrase-level or short-term 3 s measure.
Energy from 250 Hz to 4 kHz in the time-averaged mono spectrum.
Sample peak, not oversampled true peak.
Mean normalized positive magnitude change between adjacent analyzed frames.
Ungated whole-interval RMS; not integrated loudness.
Energy ratio from 5-10 kHz. A vocal detector is required before interpreting it as sibilance.
Whole-interval RMS of the same linked complementary 6.5 kHz upper split used by the deterministic de-esser. It calibrates detector level but does not identify phonemes or prove sibilance.
Mean power spectrum over Hann-windowed mono fold-down frames; source separation and masking are not represented.
Geometric-to-arithmetic mean of the averaged power spectrum; not a direct noise or quality score.
Frequency below which 85% of averaged spectral energy lies.
Unweighted linear fit to log-frequency power; do not treat a particular slope as universally correct.
Zero-lag whole-interval Pearson correlation; frequency-dependent phase is not represented.
Flux outlier count per second; tempo and event type are not inferred.

ITU-R BS.1770-5 Annex 2 FIR at 48 kHz; other rates use a bounded windowed-sinc estimate at >=192 kHz and >=2x. The meter is not formally conformance-tested and can under-read between evaluated phases.

crest_factor_timeline.limitation: Windowed sample-peak/RMS ratio; it does not by itself prove punch, over-compression, or quality.

positive_spectral_flux_timeline.limitation: Normalized positive magnitude flux on selected Hann-windowed mono fold-down frames. Long captures use a larger effective hop, and anti-phase stereo can cancel; it indicates change, not event identity or quality.

rms_dbfs_timeline.limitation: 200 ms windowed RMS with 50% nominal overlap; phrase and source interpretation require musical context.

variants.candidateSummary: A balanced source-aware deterministic plan; parameters scale within validated bounds and preservation constraints remain explicit.

Persist the measured preview compensation so the audition and committed processing are identical.
